baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction 'idha balaghat al-taraqi' uses a feminine verb of reaching with the collarbones as endpoint while leaving the subject unexpressed.
baseline_models.mechanism: The limit-reaching branch of B-L-G makes the collarbones a terminal boundary: an unnamed bodily or vital occupant advances until it meets the upper body's last visible station.

activation_trace.role: Reaching a limit supplies the endpoint motion and makes the collarbones function as a terminal boundary.

changed_reading.after: An unnamed bodily or vital process completes an approach to a terminal anatomical boundary.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Balaghat can mark not only travel to al-taraqi but a condition reaching severity in the body.
baseline_models.mechanism: The illness-or-hardship branch shifts the verb from simple locomotion to escalation: the collarbones become the bodily gauge at which a crisis has become extreme.

activation_trace.role: Intensification of illness or hardship supplies a severity scale whose upper bodily marker is the collarbones.

changed_reading.before: The verse depicts an object's upward movement.
changed_reading.after: The verse can depict a terminal crisis saturating the body to the level of the collarbones.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The hidden feminine subject of balaghat is open, and B-L-G itself carries a calamity branch while al-taraqi keeps the event bodily located.
baseline_models.mechanism: Instead of supplying a soul or breath as subject, the reading personifies a calamity that arrives at and occupies the collarbone threshold.

activation_trace.role: The calamity image supplies a possible eventive subject for the otherwise unexpressed feminine of balaghat.

changed_reading.before: An unstated life force reaches the collarbones.
changed_reading.after: An unstated calamity may itself be what reaches the collarbones.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus-only unnamed arrival becomes an exiting breath or vital self moving upward through the collarbone channel: N-F-S supplies emergence from the interior, and R-Q-Y supplies the precise anatomical site in which breath ascends.

activation_trace.role: Limit-reaching keeps the focus event anchored as motion toward a final bodily endpoint.
Breath emerging from the interior supplies a concrete candidate for the focus verse's omitted subject.
The collarbone through which breath ascends supplies both the anatomical channel and the upward direction.

structural_cues: The focus omits its grammatical subject, allowing the packet's breath image to fill the slot without displacing any stated noun.
The immediately following raqin activates R-Q-Y beside al-taraqi before the sequence moves to separation and conveyance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies breath emerging from the body and a collarbone in which breath ascends; I assign that breath or vital self as the hidden feminine subject and connect emergence to upward travel. A live alternative is a soul or generic life process rather than literal respiration.

changed_reading.before: An unspecified entity reaches a terminal anatomical point.
changed_reading.after: The body's breath or vital self exits upward until it reaches the collarbone passage.

context_deltas.mechanism: The B-L-G calamity branch joins the immediately preceding back-breaking faqirah, allowing that feminine calamity to continue as the subject of balaghat and to advance along a back-to-collarbone bodily axis.

activation_trace.role: The calamity sense of B-L-G keeps the proposed subject anchored in the focus verb.
The articulated vertebral column supplies the lower anatomical axis that continues toward the collarbones.
A back-breaking calamity supplies an adjacent feminine event that can carry over as balaghat's subject.

structural_cues: Faqirah in 75:25 is immediately followed by the feminine balaghat in 75:26.
The branch images place vertebrae, a broken back, and collarbones on one bodily axis.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies feminine adjacency, a back-breaking calamity, vertebrae, and the focus calamity branch; I carry faqirah across the ayah boundary as the omitted subject and give it upward bodily extension. The live alternative is that 75:26 begins a new clause with breath or soul as subject.

changed_reading.before: A life force reaches the collarbones after a calamity is anticipated.
changed_reading.after: The anticipated back-breaking calamity itself reaches through the body to the collarbones.

context_deltas.mechanism: Reaching the collarbones is not only an internal event but a socially recognized intervention threshold: severity produces an uttered search for someone able to apply a protective recitation or remedy.

activation_trace.role: Illness or hardship reaching severity makes the focus condition legible as an acute crisis.
Audible utterance externalizes recognition of the crisis and initiates the search for help.
Protective recitation supplies the kind of last intervention sought once the threshold is observed.

structural_cues: The conditional scene in 75:26 is answered immediately by the passive social utterance 'and it was said' in 75:27.
The interrogative 'who' turns the bodily marker into a search for an agent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an acute-severity image, an uttered question, and a protective-recitation branch; I make threshold recognition cause the summons. A live alternative is that raqin denotes a healer or helper without specifying incantation.

changed_reading.before: The collarbone arrival is a private physiological description.
changed_reading.after: The collarbone arrival is the observable triage point that triggers a final communal search for rescue.

context_deltas.mechanism: The collarbone limit becomes a handoff gate in a directed transfer: separation begins, bodily supports fold together, and the resulting passenger is driven toward a sovereign destination rather than merely stopping inside the body.

activation_trace.role: Reaching the limit establishes the gate at which the subsequent transfer begins.
Sovereignty and mastery supply the transfer's governing destination.
Separation between two things supplies the first state change after the focus threshold.
Wrapping one thing around another renders the body's supports folded and no longer independently mobile.
Driving and herding supply the directional force that carries the sequence beyond the bodily endpoint.

structural_cues: Ayat 75:26-30 form an uninterrupted conditional sequence from reaching, through recognition and separation, to al-masaq.
The destination phrase in 75:30 repeats the earlier 'to your Lord' endpoint of 75:12.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies limit, separation, wrapping, driving, and sovereign destination; I arrange these as a causal handoff from embodied cohesion to directed conveyance. A live alternative is that they are consecutive signs of dying without a single transfer mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The collarbones are the final location of an upward bodily movement.
changed_reading.after: The collarbones are a transfer gate: arrival there initiates separation and a compelled passage toward the governing destination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah brackets the collarbone limit with disassembly and construction operations. Gathering hard bones, possessing effective capacity, completing form, creating, and restoring life make 75:26 the endpoint of one embodied configuration, not the endpoint of operative power.

activation_trace.role: Limit-reaching supplies a real terminal boundary for the present bodily configuration.
Joining dispersed parts into one whole supplies the inverse operation to terminal bodily separation.
Hard bone supplies the durable material that can be dispersed and gathered again.
Effective capacity supplies the agency able to execute the inverse construction.
Integrity and completed form supply the result of reconstructing even fine bodily detail.
Bringing a creature into existence supplies the constructive operation that precedes and can answer bodily collapse.
The living ensouled creature supplies the state that restoration reconstitutes.
Loss of force and life names the state reached in the focus sequence but places it opposite renewed life.

structural_cues: The opening challenge in 75:3-4 asks about gathering and finely restoring the body before the focus death scene.
The closing sequence in 75:37-40 repeats formation and ends by asking about giving life to the dead.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies inverse material operations and frames the focus between them; I treat the frame as redefining what kind of limit is reached. A live alternative is that the frame confirms resurrection while leaving the local physiological reading unchanged.

changed_reading.before: Reaching the collarbones is an absolute terminal limit.
changed_reading.after: It is the terminal limit of the present bodily arrangement, enclosed by operations that can gather, reform, and reanimate it.

context_deltas.mechanism: Spatial arrival at the collarbones also becomes temporal expiry: duration, a measure that reaches its limit, and an apportioned death make the body display that a fixed term has come due.

activation_trace.role: The branch includes reaching a measured or temporal endpoint, allowing bodily location to register expiry.
A duration of time supplies the interval whose endpoint is reached.
A quantity reaching its prescribed limit supplies the logic of a term coming due.
An apportioned death supplies the terminal event governed by measure rather than accident.

structural_cues: The surah opens with the bounded Day and repeatedly asks when that Day will be.
The closing origin sequence joins apportioned generative material to the question of life after death.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies duration, measured limit, and apportioned death; I make the anatomical threshold the visible clock-face of that deadline. A live alternative is that balaghat remains only spatial and the temporal frame remains external.

changed_reading.before: A process happens to arrive at a high point in the body.
changed_reading.after: Arrival at the collarbones bodily registers that an apportioned term has reached its measure.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the message-conveyance branch of B-L-G is form-distant from a death description. It remains anchored in balaghat and gains support from the surah's images of a thing signifying, utterance, and clarification; downstream prose should render it only as a body-as-sign analogy, not as the lexical translation of 75:26.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: B-L-G at balaghat can image conveyance, while the collarbones keep that conveyance embodied rather than turning it into an independent speech theme.

activation_trace.role: Conveying a message recasts terminal bodily arrival as delivery of information.
A thing's 'saying' through its indication lets the body's condition function as nonverbal testimony.
Disclosure by speech or sign supplies the mechanism by which the terminal condition becomes legible.

changed_reading.before: The body silently undergoes terminal movement.
changed_reading.after: At the collarbones the body delivers a nonverbal terminal report, after which surrounding speech names the crisis.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The horseman-and-reins image is an odd idiom for balaghat and should not replace the focus verb's ordinary endpoint sense. It remains anchored in the exact focus branch and the later repeated driving vocabulary; downstream prose should qualify it as a kinetic analogy for compelled acceleration after the threshold.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus B-L-G branch images a rider extending reins to increase speed, while al-taraqi locates the release point in the upper body.

activation_trace.role: Extending a mount's reins to increase its run supplies acceleration at the moment the limit is reached.
Driving supplies the external force that takes over after the focus threshold.
Riding on the back supplies the transport analogy that makes the body a relinquished vehicle.

changed_reading.before: The terminal process slows into bodily stoppage at the collarbones.
changed_reading.after: Reaching the collarbones releases an accelerated, externally driven conveyance beyond the body.

strongest_changes: R-Q-Y's collarbone-through-which-breath-ascends branch resolves the omitted subject toward exiting breath or vital self.
The adjacent back-breaking faqirah keeps alive a competing feminine antecedent in which the calamity itself reaches the collarbones.
The separation-wrapping-driving sequence turns the collarbone endpoint into a handoff gate, while the surah's construction frame limits that ending to the present bodily configuration.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet made one terse, subjectless bodily threshold behave simultaneously as respiratory ascent, recognized crisis, calamity arrival, measured deadline, and the first station of directed transfer; the exact R-Q-Y and F-Q-R branch images kept the stranger readings anchored.
remaining_uncertainties: The hidden feminine subject remains genuinely open among breath, vital self, and the preceding calamity.
R-Q-Y in 75:27 may denote a healer or reciter; its collarbone branch is an activation bridge, not proof that the surface word carries every branch image here.
The body-as-message and accelerated-conveyance readings are material analogies and should not be promoted to direct lexical renderings.
